:::{#thm-entropy-chain-rule}
#### Chain rule for entropy

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$ and $Y$,

$$\entropyf{X, Y} = \entropyf{X} + \entropyf{Y \mid X}.$$

:::

::: {.proof}

With [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1$, the pair $(X, Y)$ takes a value $(x, y)$ with $\P(X=x, Y=y) > 0$,
so @thm-surprisal-chain-rule applies at $(x, y) = (X, Y)$:

$$\surprisalf{X, Y} = \surprisalf{X} + \surprisalf{Y \mid X}.$$

Both terms on the right are nonnegative (@cor-surprisal-discrete-nonnegative),
so the [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of the sum is the sum of the expectation of each term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\entropyf{X, Y}
&= \E{\surprisalf{X, Y}} \\
&= \E{\surprisalf{X}} + \E{\surprisalf{Y \mid X}} \\
&= \entropyf{X} + \entropyf{Y \mid X}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first line is @def-joint-entropy,
and the last line is @rem-entropy-expected-surprisal and @def-conditional-entropy.

:::
